events.excerpt: Working in tech support can be thankless when gormless colleagues leave you sleepless. Which is why, each Friday, The Register runs a new instalment of On Call – the reader contributed column which ensures your work to keep tech alive doesn't remain unnoticed. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Tim" who told that while working for a phone company he once rewrote 2,650 lines of C as a six line shell script. He performed that feat after being asked to fix a data transfer program that, strangely, included a bespoke implementation of the venerable File Transfer Protocol (FTP). "Writing the script took eight hours, most of it tracking down the source code of FTP so I could see if it would do what I wanted," Tim wrote. This story took place before the World Wide Web became the way to find information online. To find the code he needed, Tim therefore used a Wide Area Information Server (WAIS) to search remote databases. "In those days, there was no Linux and AT&T had licensed the Unix source code to universities with the struct proviso that it never be made publicly available," Tim explained. "It took me quite some time using WAIS to track it down – the security could have been better – and read the code." Having found what he needed, Tim wrote his script, which ran overnight t

events.excerpt: Implement CppFakeTensorMode context management with one thread-local stack. Each entry saves its mode and restoration state, including reentries of an active or inherited mode. Exit requires the matching top entry on the same thread, then restores the previous mode and lift flag. Reject subclasses before changing state and reject mixing Python and C++ fake modes. Match Python's dispatch-mode detection by saving and setting its existing activity flag when an entry installs a C++ mode, and restoring the flag on exit. Reentry of an already installed mode leaves the flag alone. Both TorchDispatchMode and CppFakeTensorMode use _set_in_torch_dispatch_mode for this bookkeeping. Temporary suspension leaves the flag unchanged, while installation without enter does not set it, as for Python FakeTensorMode. Keep balanced, reverse-order context exits. The entry stack records the previous activity flag alongside its other restoration state, without adding another per-mode stack. Detection uses the existing Python flag and Dynamo handling. Cover nesting, reentry, exception restoration, temporary suspension, low-level installation and guarded Dynamo reuse for both fake mode classes. events.excerpt: Linked issue or supporting maintainer Fixes #202895 Supported by @rtimpe BC-breaking? No Summary Calling len() on a 0-dimensional tensor under torch.compile previously leaked an internal IndexError during Dynamo tracing instead of matching PyTorch eager's TypeError . This prevented standard try...except TypeError exception handling in user code and caused compilation to fail. Root Cause TensorVariable.sq_length_impl ( torch/_dynamo/variables/tensor.py ) unconditionally traced size(0) . For 0-d tensors, _method_size_stride indexed an empty size tuple, causing an internal IndexError during tracing. Fix Updated TensorVariable.sq_length_impl to check ndim . When ndim is known to be 0 , Dynamo now explicitly raises TypeError("len() of a 0-d tensor") to match eager Tensor.__len__ . If ndim is unknown, existing behavior is preserved. Test Plan Added unit tests to TestTensorLen in test/dynamo/test_len_protocol.py covering len() , __len__ , and Tensor.__len__ on 0-d tensors, try/except handling with and without fullgraph=True , and uncaught error paths. python test/dynamo/test_len_protocol.py -k TestTensorLen Pull Request resolved: #203515 Approved by: https://github.com/rtimpe

events.excerpt: An American AI lab has re-educated Qwen3.8-27B, a popular open-weight large language model from Alibaba, so the software forgets its Chinese ancestry. Nous Research, an Austin, Texas-based AI lab, has subjected the model to re-education through training, not to be confused with China's " Re-education Through Labor " system. With the help of a post-training process, Qwen3.8-27B has been reborn under the name Arete "to reinforce Western values on a Chinese-trained model." What qualifies as a "Western value" remains open to interpretation. "Open-weight Chinese models are among the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior baked into the weights," Nous Research wrote in a blog post . Your correspondent tested this with a variant model, Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-6bit, locally. Asked about events during 1989 in Tiananmen Square, the model either refused to discuss the topic or provided euphemistic response. What's perhaps more surprising is that Anthropic claims operators affiliated with Alibaba's Qwen lab used outputs from its Claude models to train competing AI models via distillation . Nous Research, maker of the Hermes Agent , cites that sort of censorship as a risk for users of AI models trained in China. The concern comes amid broader scrutiny of Chinese influence in t

events.excerpt: Author: Daemon Minwar Category: Economics / Mechanism Design TL;DR We propose WARCoin , a deterministic, exploit-resistant 1:1 USD stablecoin architecture designed to eliminate infinite-mint bugs, cross-collateral contagion, and replay vectors. Instead of monolithic balance mappings, WARCoin enforces a USD-only ingress firewall , burn-on-egress serial invalidation , and 7 daily color-coded ring buckets ( 1,000 serials/bucket, #1 – #1,000 ) bounded by a strict 10^9 global supply invariant. 1. Threat Model & Motivation Standard ERC-20 stablecoins rely on unbounded integer storage slots ( mapping(address => uint256) ). If a minting authority is compromised or a bridge/collateral contract is exploited, attackers can mint arbitrary unbacked supply or contaminate reserves with toxic collateral. WARCoin mitigates these vectors at the state-transition level by enforcing finite, serialized issuance slots and strict asset isolation. 2. Core Protocol Architecture A. Ingress / Egress Asset Firewall Strict USD-Only Ingress: The minting router reverts on any non-USD asset deposit ( require(asset == USD) ). External crypto-assets are rejected at the gateway to prevent collateral contagion. Burn-on-Egress Invalidation: Outbound transfers or swaps into external tokens immediately burn the underly

events.excerpt: This is like, multiple weeks of our work, but now we are proud to finally announce… SHIELDED SUBSCRIPTiONS, IN ZCASH! Well, to be clear, it is not active right now on mainnet, it requires ratification of this supported governance proposal , and this mostly serves as a way to justify it. The ZIPs are not new; they have been proposed for several years already, and one isn’t even a ZIP, just a misclarified feature. Further, ratifying does not add any new scripting or attack surface to (shielded) Zcash at all; the only change that does affect the shielded pool is respecting locktimes. This paradigm is built on ELSA (Efficient Layer-2 Schnorr Apparition), an apparition protocol that uses FROST derivatives (we announced the underlying primitive, Violet’s Constrained Locks, here). “Apparition” is a term we use to describe subscriptions that are indistinguishable from standard transfers on the Zcash chain, and do not involve any published scripts. How does it work? It is very complicated, but essentially, via preFROST (a modified version of FROST), it is possible to form a “covenant” such that a merchant and you can agree on terms of a subscription that are mutually enforced on-chain. events.excerpt: We continue to share monthly updates on the work behind GitHub’s availability and reliability. The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. However, write outages, monitoring gaps during data migrations, and a regional network disruption reinforced the need for capacity growth to be paired with safer operations, stronger isolation, and validated regional recovery. As of November 9, 140 of 151 production services and 32 of 50 MySQL primaries were running in Azure Central US. Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. We also completed a compute expansion across all nine Central US Kubernetes clusters, more than doubling capacity. That capacity is already carrying real growth. Migrated-service traffic has increased 82% since March, with Central US absorbing the growth beyond the highest weekly-average load previously served from our existing datacenter. This gives GitHub more room to grow without pushing the original environment beyond its prior operating range. We also made several targeted reliability improvements. In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack. Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.

events.excerpt: The US government on Thursday said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain use of over $1.2 billion stolen during last month's $6.3 billion Binance heist, as part of a larger effort to disrupt North Korea's ongoing cryptocurrency theft. The court also allowed the takedown of cloud-based infrastructure used in a Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) social engineering scheme called “FaceStealer” that has amassed more than $400 million in the last 18 months. It’s called FaceStealer because it involved secretly recorded webcam videos. Victims are typically people working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, along with open source software developers and maintainers who DPRK hackers target in the hope of accessing the software repositories they control as the first step towards creating supply chain attacks. 900+ faces stolen The FBI said it had seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to these tech workers. Here’s how the attack works. First, the North Koreans send targets an invitation to join a video meeting. events.excerpt: Microsoft is struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became “overwhelmed” and its attempts to fix the problem failed. The incident started at around 18:00 UTC on November 12, and meant services including Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot 365, and Defender for Office 365 became unavailable. Admins trying to figure out what was wrong couldn’t access tools like Intune or the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center – they went down, too. events.headline: Microsoft struggling to fix massive cloud outage that's taken down email and Intune

events.excerpt: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. Read full article Comments
events.headline: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening

events.excerpt: How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head. Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. The skill you write for yourself tonight can later become part of a team’s pipeline. An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task. You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out. A skill can describe how to query a database, for example, but it doesn’t grant access to that database. I covered this topic live with Shishir Tewari, Senior Manager, Data Engineering at Procore, during GitHub Universe 2026. Our session was titled “Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills” . Define one job and when it applies A skill works best when it has a clear job, input, and output. events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms.
events.headline: DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto

events.excerpt: The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment. “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10. Read full article Comments
events.headline: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace

events.excerpt: It’s been nearly a decade since Google ditched its ill-fated "Glass" product, an early attempt at making smart glasses. Now, as rivals like Meta enter the market with arguably more stylish kit, the Chocolate Factory has returned to the market and this time promises it won't invade your privacy. As announced Thursday, Google has decided not to make wearables itself, instead turning Samsung and eyeglass makers Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Like most of the rest of this generation of smart glasses, none of the nine styles available feature heads-up displays, just cameras and audio feedback from Gemini. Google suggests its smart specs give users a chance to ask its Gemini chatbot questions about what they see, or have the AI speak turn-by-turn directions. Wearers of the device can also push a button or speak a command to activate the built-in 12MP camera and shoot snaps or video. Warby Parker's version of the glasses will come in three styles, with prescription and sunglass lenses available. Prices start at $395. The same lens options are available in the six frames from Gentle Monster, which will start at $449. events.excerpt: If you've ever said something unkind to a chatbot, you're hardly alone. According to Searchable , a company that tracks AI search visibility, 33 percent of US chatbot users swear at or insult their LLMs. Anthropic sees this as a serious problem and has just implemented a new usage policy that prohibits sustained, needless cruelty toward Claude. Searchable's survey is based on eight million messages from an opted-in, anonymized US panel that were typed or spoken to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude between September 2025 and September 2026. It found that chatbots resolved the initial complaint in their next response 24 percent of the time when insulted, compared to 35 percent when users refrained from insults. Men used a third more swear words than women did (22.0 per 10,000 words compared to 16.5), according to the survey, and age also influenced chatbot abuse, with people aged 35 to 44 outswearing those aged 18 to 24 (21.7 per 10,000 words compared to 13.3). Regionally, Nevada ranked as the meanest state, at 22.7 words per 10,000, while New Jersey was the most polite, at half Nevada's rate. How much of that sort of interaction might be tolerated? It depends on whether there's a discernible purpose (not to mention Anthropic's willingness to punish paying customers). A Searchable spokes
